chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There was a man who used to sell oil, and he loved the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with intense love. Whenever he intended to go for his business needs, he would not leave until he looked at the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). This was known about him, for when he came, he would stretch himself out so that he could look at him. It happened one day that he came to him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stretched out to him until he looked at him, then he went away for his business needs.

He did not take long before he returned. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw him do that, he gestured to him with his hand, saying, 'Sit.' So he sat in front of him. He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What is the matter? You have done something today that you had not done before.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, by the One who sent you with the Truth as a Prophet, a portion of your remembrance overwhelmed my heart to the extent that I could not go about my business until I returned to you.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated for him and wished him well.

Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) waited a few days but did not see him. When he missed him, he asked about him, and it was said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have not seen him for days.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) put on his shoes, and his companions put on theirs with him, and they set out until they came to the oil market. They found the man's shop empty, with no one in it. So he asked his neighbors about him. They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, he died. He was indeed trustworthy and truthful among us, except that he had a peculiar habit.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'And what was that?' They said, 'He used to exhaust himself following the women.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'May Allah have mercy upon him. By Allah, he used to love me with such love that even if he had been a slave trader, Allah would forgive him.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) respond to a companion's unique habit of loving him intensely?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *al-hubb* (love) as a potent spiritual force that can expiate minor sins or even significant character flaws, such as the man's tendency to follow women. The Prophet’s declaration that his love was sufficient for forgiveness, even if he were a 'slave trader' (*nakhhas*), highlights the transformative power of sincere devotion in Shia theology. This narrative underscores that intense emotional connection to the Prophet can serve as a means of spiritual purification, balancing human imperfections with divine grace.
